summary: An excerpt from Book 11 (part 102) of a fiction work, apparently Kate Douglas Wiggin's Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm. Rebecca waits by a window as Huldah returns from the woods with Mr. Aladdin, and she feels a sudden jealous pang over her place in his friendship. Aladdin then visits Rebecca's room, where they talk of school matters, and he explains that he became a school trustee in memory of his mother, whose last happy years were spent at the school. The passage ends with Aladdin noting his age as thirty-two.
one_line: Rebecca, jealous of Huldah's time with Mr. Aladdin, talks with him in her room and explains his trusteeship of the school.
key_facts: Huldah and Mr. Aladdin are seen coming up the path through the woods, with Huldah wearing a black and white veil and high-heeled shoes.
Rebecca feels a sudden 'storm in her heart' at the thought of giving up her share of Mr. Aladdin's friendship to Huldah.
Rebecca realizes Emma Jane has only ever held a secondary place in Mr. Aladdin's regard.
Mr. Aladdin enters the room after Miss Maxwell tells him that Miss Rebecca Randall is there.
Mr. Aladdin admits he cannot remember the name of the rich blacksmith's daughter, Emma Jane.
Rebecca tells Mr. Aladdin that Emma Jane is her room-mate.
Mr. Aladdin had not seen Rebecca for several months and had already inquired about her progress from Mr. Morrison.
Mr. Aladdin says he must drive to Portland for a meeting of railway directors the next day.
Mr. Aladdin says he always takes the opportunity of visiting the school to give advice on its educational and financial affairs.
Rebecca says it seems funny for Mr. Aladdin to be a school trustee.
Mr. Aladdin says he accepted the trusteeship in memory of his poor little mother, whose last happy years were spent at the school.
Mr. Aladdin states that he is thirty-two years old.
